title: The module of differentials of a scheme over its base equals the module of differentials over its relative Frobenius factor
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a scheme X over S in characteristic p, the module of Kaehler differentials Omega_{X/S} equals Omega_{X/X^(p)}, where X^(p) is the relative Frobenius factor. The proof translates to algebra: for A -> B in characteristic p with B' = B otimes_{A, F_A} A and the Frobenius-linear map F : B' -> B, it suffices to show Omega_{B/A} = Omega_{B/B'}; this follows because the universal derivation d satisfies d(b^p a) = 0, so d is a B'-derivation (proof lines 7143-7150). H2: the identification of the universal derivation as a derivation over the Frobenius factor and its functorial characterization constitute the non-routine step.
